newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Vierfontein leaps on restructuring news.
newsitem.headline: Vierfontein leaps on restructuring news.

text.p: Shares in Vierfontein Colliery Ltd (VCL), a South African coal firm, leapt on Monday on news of a possible restructuring which could see a new business put into VCL.
By 1350 GMT VCL had surged over 41 percent or 25 cents to 85 cents, equalling its best level this year and making it the biggest percentage gainer on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on the day.
"The share doesn't trade very much. It's up on the cautionary," one share dealer said.
VCL said earlier that Ben Nevis Holdings Ltd (BNH) had approached it with proposals which could result in a new business being placed in VCL.

BNH had already acquired an 18 percent shareholding in VCL and proposes to make a fully guaranteed cash offer to acquire all existing VCL shares at a price of no less than 25 cents a share, the coal firm said.
VCL added that it will need to hold discussion with various interested parties on the proposals.
